claims.text: Partial substitution of Ta with additional Ti in TiVNbTa will improve strength retention at 1273 K.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy is a single-phase BCC material with a dendritic microstructure.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 800 MPa at lower temperatures.
The initial TiVNbTa alloy has a yield strength of approximately 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Ta is to be partially replaced by Ti while the remaining formulation and processing conditions are held constant.
Increasing Ti at the expense of Ta will enhance lattice distortion and solid-solution strengthening.
Increasing Ti at the expense of Ta may stabilize the BCC structure.
Increasing Ti at the expense of Ta may slow diffusion kinetics.
Greater lattice distortion raises the activation energy for dislocation motion.
Sluggish diffusion caused by the substitution will impede dislocation slip and grain-boundary mobility.
Impeded dislocation slip and grain-boundary mobility will reduce high-temperature creep and softening.
At 1273 K, the modified alloy may reach a yield strength of approximately 400 MPa rather than the baseline value of approximately 330 MPa.
The modified alloy is expected to retain ductility comparable to that of the baseline alloy.
The baseline alloy has a compressive strength of approximately 423 MPa at 30% strain and 1273 K.
The proposed improvement is limited to conditions around 1273 K and is not established at other temperatures or strain rates.
A gain of less than approximately 15% in 1273 K yield strength across all substituted alloys, or a gain accompanied by significant loss of ductility or phase stability, would falsify the hypothesis.
